page: Amazon Web Services c7a.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 1 physical core and 1 virtual CPU running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local NVMe SSD storage, and does not include any bundled GPUs or baseline network bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. However, because the instance is limited to a single dedicated core, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show mixed results, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% at 147.72 GB/sec, while large block write bandwidth achieves an average rating at 28.35 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations, including gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, perform at average levels.

From a resource density and cost efficiency perspective, the c7a.medium offers a dedicated hardware profile suitable for entry-level compute workloads without the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. However, users face tradeoffs due to the lack of local storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, simple web serving, and small-scale development or testing environments that require dedicated CPU execution but do not demand high memory or multi-threaded performance.
